analysis.title: GS Wilson - weekly mash 9 Oct 2026
key_insights: Equity 'momentum' factor has been a headwind since the end of Q2, which is hurting investor performance and client sentiment. US Fundamental Long/Short hedge fund net length is in the 1st percentile on a 1-year lookback.

None of the week's major newsflow was particularly negative apart from the Middle East, yet investors treated headlines as 'tape bombs'. Longer-dated yields remain tightly correlated to 12-month forward crude prices.

Headlines were read negatively: Le Pen's fiscal discipline talk (market focused on how hard 2% deficit targets would be), SpaceX and Broadcom financing (market focused on competition for capital and crowding out of sovereign demand), AI model companies showing conservative net revenue estimates (read as possible demand weakness), and Samsung and TSMC strong results (not rewarded given uncertainty on cycle duration and post-Midterms US policy).

Higher rates make it harder for equities to progress. A historic investment cycle means sovereigns now compete with private sector capex for funding, and investors' willingness to finance the AI buildout requires ever-higher concessions to fund public sector liabilities.
The rise in rates is real-rate led: 98bps of the 108bps 10-year sell-off has been real rates. Private sector balance sheets are in fine shape (aggregate listed company leverage by region).
The equity vs rates correlation (EuroStoxx vs 10-year bunds) has flipped to a level not seen since the 1990s.
Ireland highlighted as one of the most remarkable balance sheet turnarounds in modern economic history, relevant as sovereign funding returns to focus.
Next week CPI is key as a possible catalyst to break momentum in the broad fixed income sell-off, but equities and the AI investment story drive the macro, so Q3 earnings matter most.

Europe: GS forecasts 22% 2H'26 EPS growth, with the market on 13x earnings, 5.5% FCF yield, steeply negative equity supply, no bad breadth issues and M&A at levels not seen since pre-GFC. Stocks have traded with a strong correlation to EPS revisions YTD.

US: GS forecasts 27% clean EPS growth in Q3, the cycle high, with growth decelerating over the following 3 quarters. This is also the peak quarter of narrowness: the top 10 contributors make up 68% of SPX EPS growth (48% last quarter, 54% est. Q4), and Micron and Nvidia make up half of the 68%.

Core view: AI investment is the central driver of cross-asset price behavior. If investment shows no let-up, a major yield reversal is not expected, but stable energy prices would relieve the bond sell-off and allow equities to rally to year-end.

Hyperscaler capex growth is likely to peak this quarter, well above 100%, and cloud revenue backlog growth will exceed that. Revenue lags spend but will converge toward those growth rates in coming quarters. Market narrowness may get more extreme as leadership shifts from AI spend beneficiaries to the biggest AI investors.

sector_views.rationale: Leadership may flip from AI spend beneficiaries to the biggest AI investors as ROI shows. Revenue growth is expected to converge toward capex growth rates.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment demand is insatiable, Q3 US EPS growth is forecast at 27%, hyperscaler capex and cloud backlog growth are above 100%, and stable energy prices would relieve the bond sell-off and let equities rally to year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher real rates and sovereign funding competition from the AI investment cycle weigh on equities. Equity vs rates correlation has flipped to a level not seen since the 1990s, and market narrowness is extreme.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Investment activity showing signs of let-up would remove the support, and a further rise in crude prices would keep long-dated yields rising.
